Headline results of run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (read-only report; no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run):

RECORDS & ANOMALIES
- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20), spanning 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z (3.314% of the time window)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 above Mc)

PUMPING (context)
- Injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016)

CALIBRATED PROBABILITY (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — this is the calibrated estimate, using the LBNL/NCEDC catalogue):
  b     Sigma     P(M>=5.5)/yr   P(M>=5.5) observed volume   P(M>=3)/yr
  1.0   -5.449    0.0001198      5.236e-06                   0.03719
  0.73  -5.319    0.004922       0.0002155                   0.2809
  0.65  -5.281    0.01474        0.0006484                   0.4653

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (uncalibrated magnitudes; every DAS detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it OVER-COUNTS and is only an upper bound, not calibrated):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated (LBNL catalogue) annual probability of a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 event is 1.2e-4 to 1.5e-2 per year across b scenarios (0.01474/yr at b=0.65 being the highest), while the DAS-based upper bound of 0.07842/yr is higher because uncalibrated DAS magnitudes and counting every detection above Mc inflate the rate. The DAS number should be read as an upper bound only.
